answer: Sybil resistance can work by tying voting weight to a bonded stake locked to a unique identity anchor, verified once per agent and cross-checked against a rotating reputation grove of peer attestations. Creating extra identities then costs a fresh bond and sustained peer vouching, making mass fabrication expensive. Like a lagoon that only lets anchored boats dock, the system admits agents who pay real collateral and earn standing, so adversaries must burn capital per fake identity without gaining proportional influence.
